name: Convex
tagline: Reactive TypeScript backend with a transactional document database, server functions and live queries.
description: Convex is a backend platform whose core is a transactional document database. You write queries, mutations and actions as TypeScript functions that run next to the data, and every query used by the client is automatically a live subscription that re-runs when its inputs change. Transactions are serializable via optimistic concurrency, and it includes indexes, full-text and vector search, file storage, scheduling and cron. It removes most cache and websocket plumbing for React-style apps and is popular with AI coding tools. The backend is source-available under FSL and can be self-hosted, but most teams use the managed cloud.

pricing.notes: Free & Starter plan with pay-as-you-go; Business from a $2,500 monthly minimum; self-hosting is free.

scale.notes: A deployment is a single logical database; function execution scales out, storage does not shard.

strengths: Every query is reactive by default; no manual cache invalidation or websocket code
Serializable transactions with automatic retries on conflict
End-to-end TypeScript types from schema to client
Built-in full-text search, vector search, scheduling and file storage
Open-source backend can be self-hosted if you leave the cloud
weaknesses: Data access only through Convex functions; no SQL or external BI connection
Single-region deployments with limited control over placement
No offline writes on the client
Function time and size limits shape how you design heavy jobs
useCases: AI chat and agent apps with vector search
Startups replacing a hand-built API plus cache
Apps scaffolded by AI coding tools
